---

In the context of your contract, this part:

> "**Customer maintains CRM access and does not significantly delay campaign approvals, call reviews, or onboarding processes**"

means that the **Customer (Andrea)** must:

1. **CRM Access**: Keep access to the Customer Relationship Management system (like Acquisity or High Level) active and available to the Supplier for campaign management and performance tracking.

2. **Campaign Approvals**: Respond in a timely manner to requests from the Supplier to approve ad creatives, messaging, or campaign elements. Delays here can hold up the launch or performance optimization.

3. **Call Reviews**: Participate in, or allow, the review of recorded or live sales/consultation calls so the Supplier can analyze performance and improve scripts or booking processes.

4. **Onboarding Processes**: Complete all required setup tasks—like uploading necessary information, attending kickoff meetings, and configuring tools—promptly during the initial onboarding window.

If the Customer is slow or unresponsive in any of these areas, the **guarantee of 15 qualified consults per month within 90 days** could be voided, since those delays would affect the Supplier’s ability to deliver results.

A **setup fee** is a **one-time charge** paid at the beginning of a service agreement to cover the initial work required to get a project or system up and running.

---

### In your context, a setup fee typically covers:
- CRM configuration  
- Landing page or funnel buildout  
- Domain warming and email integration  
- Ad account audits or creative development  
- Script writing, automations, and reporting setup  

---

### Key Points:
- Charged **once**, usually before services begin  
- Covers **foundational work** needed to launch campaigns or systems  
- Is **separate from the monthly retainer or performance fees**

This Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and entered into on the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”). 
Meanings

This supply of services agreement, including all schedules and any attachments.


“Confidential Information”
In relation to either party, any information (whether or not stated to be confidential or marked as such) disclosed to the other party, or which the other party obtains from any information disclosed to it, either orally, in writing, or by any other means, in connection with this Agreement.
- “Deliverables”  
  All documents, items, plans, products, goods, and materials supplied by the Supplier in connection with the Services, in any form or media, including methodologies, ideas, designs, computer programs, data, disks, tapes, and reports, developed or produced by the Supplier (or its agents, subcontractors, consultants, and employees).
- “DPA”  
  The data processing agreement attached as Schedule 5, which is incorporated by reference into this Agreement.
- “Effective Date”  
  The date on which the last party signs this Agreement.
- “Equipment”  
  Any equipment, systems, tools, cabling, items, materials, or facilities used or required (whether directly or indirectly) by the Supplier or its subcontractors in the supply of the Services.
- “Intellectual Property Rights”  
  Patents, rights to inventions, copyright and related rights, trade marks, trade names, domain names, rights in get-up, goodwill or to sue for passing off, rights in designs, rights in computer software, database rights, moral rights, topography rights, and any other intellectual property rights, in each case whether registered or unregistered and including all applications, renewals, or extensions of such rights, and all similar or equivalent rights or forms of protection existing now or in the future.
- “Services”

- “Service Charges”  
  The charges for the Services as set out in Schedule 2 of this Agreement.
- “Service Levels”  
  The service levels, standards, or performance targets set out in Schedule 3 of this Agreement.
- “Specification”  
  The description or specification for the Services as set out in Schedule 1 and as may be amended in writing by the parties in accordance with clause 8 (Change Control).
- “Working Day” (sometimes referred to as “Business Day”)  
  - If governed by UK law: any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in England and Wales.  
  - If governed by US law: any day (other than a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday) on which commercial banks are generally open for business in the relevant state.
In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:
1. The singular includes the plural and vice versa.
2. References to clauses, schedules, and appendices are to clauses, schedules, and appendices of this Agreement.
3. A reference to a person includes firms, companies, government entities, trusts, and partnerships.

The word **"arrears"** means **after the work or service has been completed**, rather than in advance.

So when your contract says:

> “Revenue share invoiced monthly **in arrears** based on verified new client revenue.”

It means that the **5% revenue share** will be calculated and billed **after** each month ends—once the new client revenue from that month can be confirmed.

### Example:
If Andrea earns $20,000 in new client revenue from July’s campaigns, you would invoice her **in early August** for 5% of that ($1,000).

It’s the opposite of **"in advance"**, where payment would be due before results are delivered.

A **retainer** is a fixed, recurring fee paid in advance to secure ongoing access to a professional’s services.

### In simple terms:
It’s a **monthly (or regular) payment** made to reserve your time, expertise, or resources—regardless of how much or little work is done that month.

---

### Common uses:
- In your case, a **retainer** might cover ongoing services like ad management, lead generation, strategy consulting, or campaign oversight.
- The client pays this fee to keep you "on call" or engaged for an agreed period.

---

### Key Points:
- **Paid up front** (usually monthly)
- **Secures priority** access to services
- May include a set number of hours or deliverables—or simply guarantee ongoing support

These two clauses in the contract define the financial limits of liability for both parties—essentially capping how much money one party could be required to pay the other in the event of a problem, mistake, or legal issue.

Here’s what they mean in plain English:

---

**Clause 8.3:**
> *“The Supplier’s total liability shall not exceed the Charges paid in the 6 months preceding the claim.”*

- If the Customer (Andrea/PRESTIGE) brings a legal claim against the Supplier (Bethany/New Era Intel), the most the Supplier could be held financially responsible for is the amount the Customer has paid for services in the **six months prior to the issue or claim**.
- For example: If the Customer paid $4,500/month, and brought a claim in month 7, the maximum liability would be 6 months x $4,500 = **$27,000**.

---

**Clause 8.4:**
> *“Each party’s total aggregate liability for all claims shall not exceed $20,000.”*

- This sets an **absolute cap of $20,000** for **all claims combined**, regardless of how much has been paid or how many claims are made.
- So even if the 6-month total under 8.3 is higher (like $27,000), the **maximum payout from either party is limited to $20,000 total**.

---

### Summary:
- **Clause 8.3** limits liability based on recent payments.
- **Clause 8.4** puts a **firm ceiling of $20,000** on liability—whichever is **lower** will apply.
